title: Derived dg-module tensor and its flat bar model
statement:
Use the cochain convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$ as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Let $\mathcal B$ be such a category, $G$ a right dg $\mathcal B$-module and $F$ a left dg $\mathcal B$-module: their values are cochain complexes, with unital associative chain-map actions $G(V)\otimes\mathcal B(U,V)\to G(U)$ and $\mathcal B(U,V)\otimes F(U)\to F(V)$. Their balanced tensor is the direct sum $\bigoplus_U G(U)\otimes F(U)$ modulo $(ga)\otimes f=g\otimes(af)$. A semi-free module has an exhaustive increasing filtration starting at zero, split on underlying graded modules, whose successive dg quotients are direct sums of shifted representables; such replacements exist by [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement], also for left modules by passage to the opposite category. Tensoring either semi-free input with an objectwise quasi-isomorphism of the other input is a quasi-isomorphism. If $P\to G$ and $Q\to F$ are semi-free replacements, then
$$P\otimes_{\mathcal B}F\ \longleftarrow\ P\otimes_{\mathcal B}Q\ \longrightarrow\ G\otimes_{\mathcal B}Q$$
are quasi-isomorphisms. They define the derived balanced tensor, natural in the two modules and invariant under objectwise quasi-isomorphisms in both inputs.

Assume in addition that every $\mathcal B(U,V)$ is homotopically flat over $\mathbf Z$, meaning its tensor with any acyclic complex is acyclic, and that at least one of $F,G$ is objectwise homotopically flat over $\mathbf Z$. The unnormalized two-sided bar total complex $B(G,\mathcal B,F)$ represents $G\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal B}F$. Its simplicial degree $n\geq0$ is
$$\bigoplus_{U_0,\ldots,U_n}G(U_n)\otimes\mathcal B(U_{n-1},U_n)\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathcal B(U_0,U_1)\otimes F(U_0),$$
Write this tensor complex as $V_n$ and put $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}V_n[n]$, so simplicial degree $n$ lowers the cochain degree by $n$. On $V_n[n]$ the internal differential is $(-1)^n d_{V_n}$. For $n\geq1$ its other component is $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i\partial_i:V_n[n]\to V_{n-1}[n-1]$: numbering the factors from the left by $0,\ldots,n+1$, $\partial_i$ merges adjacent factors $i,i+1$ by the right action when $i=0$, composition when $0<i<n$, and the left action when $i=n$. This component is zero on $V_0$. Degeneracies insert units. The augmentation to $G\otimes_{\mathcal B}F$ is the quotient map on $V_0$ and zero on $V_n$ for $n>0$. The comparison with the derived balanced tensor is natural in module maps. The complex $B[1]$, rather than $B$, has $n+1$ suspensions in the summand indexed by $V_n$.

source.place: Drinfeld §§14.3-14.8 (balanced tensor, semi-free homotopical flatness), §3.6(i) (bar model under flatness), and §1.3.1. Supports prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint proof paragraph 2: derived evaluation of the restricted representable modules.

proof.text: For the right representable $h_X(U)=\mathcal B(U,X)$, the map $h_X\otimes_{\mathcal B}F\to F(X)$ sends $a\otimes f$ to $af$. Its inverse sends $f$ to $1_X\otimes f$: the balanced relation gives $a\otimes f=1_X\otimes af$. Both maps commute with the differential by the chain-map action and $d1_X=0$. Likewise $G\otimes_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B(X,-)\cong G(X)$ by $g\otimes a\mapsto ga$, inverse $g\mapsto g\otimes1_X$. For a right shift $h_X[k]$, the evaluation $a\otimes f\mapsto af$ identifies $h_X[k]\otimes_{\mathcal B}F$ with $F(X)[k]$. For a left shift $L[k]$, the shifted left action is $a\cdot y=(-1)^{k|a|}ay$; the map $g\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{k|g|}g\otimes y$ identifies $G\otimes_{\mathcal B}L[k]$ with $(G\otimes_{\mathcal B}L)[k]$. These formulas respect the balanced relation and the shifted differentials. Tensor distributes over direct sums because every tensor and every balanced relation has finite support. Thus sums of shifted representables give sums of shifted evaluations. All sums are indexed by sets, since the object set is small in the fixed universe.

source.place: Tag 09LM (dga-lemma-tensor), several-object evaluation checked directly; Drinfeld 14.4 for orientation.

proof.text: We will repeatedly use this elementary acyclicity argument. In a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to A\to C\to D\to0$ with $A,D$ acyclic, a cycle $z\in C$ maps to $d\bar y$ in $D$; lift $\bar y$ to $y\in C$, then $z-dy$ is a cycle in $A$ and hence a boundary. Thus $C$ is acyclic. A direct sum of acyclic complexes is acyclic because a cycle has finite support, so one may choose primitives in its finitely many nonzero components. The union of an increasing sequence of acyclic subcomplexes is acyclic because every cycle belongs to a stage and bounds there. For the cone test, write $\operatorname{Cone}(u)^r=C^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ with $d(c,a)=(dc+u(a),-da)$, as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If the cone is acyclic, every cycle $(c,0)$ bounds $(y,b)$, so $db=0$ and $c=dy+u(b)$, proving surjectivity of $H(u)$. If $da=0$ and $u(a)=dc$, the cone cycle $(-c,a)$ bounds, so $a$ is a boundary, proving injectivity. Conversely assume $H(u)$ is bijective and $(c,a)$ is a cone cycle. Since $u(a)=-dc$, injectivity gives $a=db$. The element $c+u(b)$ is closed; surjectivity gives a closed $e$ and a $y$ with $c+u(b)=u(e)+dy$. Then $(c,a)=d(y,e-b)$. This proves the cone criterion directly for complexes of abelian groups, including objectwise module cones.

source.place: Tag 09S3 (dga-lemma-functoriality-bc), filtration acyclicity argument; cone criterion proved directly by the displayed cycles with the cone convention of def-weil-abstract-derived-category.

proof.text: Let $P$ be semi-free and $N$ an objectwise acyclic left module. Tensor the graded-split filtration $P_i$ with $N$. The graded splitting ensures that $P_i\otimes_{\mathcal B}N\to P_{i+1}\otimes_{\mathcal B}N$ is injective and the quotient is $(P_{i+1}/P_i)\otimes_{\mathcal B}N$: the graded retraction and the universal balanced relations give the direct-sum decomposition before taking the differential. By step 1 each quotient is a direct sum of shifted complexes $N(X)$, hence acyclic. Starting with $P_0=0$, step 2 proves acyclicity at every stage and at the union. That union is $P\otimes_{\mathcal B}N$: each tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors from some $P_i$, and each finite set of balanced relations occurs at a later common stage. For an objectwise quasi-isomorphism $u:F\to F'$, the chain isomorphism $P\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(u)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(P\otimes u)$ is identity on the $P\otimes F'$ summand and sends $x\otimes a$ in $P\otimes F[1]$ to $(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes a$ in $(P\otimes F)[1]$. The balanced relations respect this sign because a left shift twists its action by $(-1)^{|a|}$; substitution in the cone differential verifies the isomorphism. Apply what was just proved to $N=\operatorname{Cone}(u)$, then the cone test of step 2. This proves $P\otimes_{\mathcal B}u$ is a quasi-isomorphism without any flatness assumption on the mapping complexes. For the left-input assertion, use the graded opposite category: composition reverses with the Koszul sign, a left $\mathcal B$-module $L$ becomes a right $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$-module by $\ell\cdot a=(-1)^{|\ell||a|}a\ell$, and a right module $M$ becomes a left one by $a\cdot m=(-1)^{|a||m|}ma$. The map $m\otimes\ell\mapsto(-1)^{|m||\ell|}\ell\otimes m$ is a chain isomorphism $M\otimes_{\mathcal B}L\cong L\otimes_{\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}}M$: substitution verifies both the relation and the differential. A semi-free left input is semi-free on the right over the opposite category; the right-input assertion there therefore gives the left-input assertion here.

source.place: Tag 09S3 (dga-lemma-functoriality-bc), proof by split property-(P) filtration, expanded for dg categories; also Tag 0GZ2 (dga-lemma-compute-bc).

proof.text: Choose $p:P\to G$ and $q:Q\to F$ by [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement], applying it also to $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Step 3 applied to $q$ with right input $P$ gives $P\otimes q$, and its left-input version applied to $p$ with input $Q$ gives $p\otimes Q$. These are exactly the two arrows in the displayed span, and both are quasi-isomorphisms. We may thus use $P\otimes Q$, $P\otimes F$, or $G\otimes Q$ as the same object of $D(\mathbf Z)$.

Here are the map and independence checks for this construction, rather than just its object values. By [lem-coef-dg-semi-free-homotopically-projective], for a semi-free $P$ the complex $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,N)$ is acyclic whenever $N$ is objectwise acyclic. For any quasi-isomorphism $s:N\to N'$, the cone of $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,s)$ identifies with $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,\operatorname{Cone}(s))$ by the two summands. The cone test gives an isomorphism on $H^0$. Hence, for a module map $f:G\to G'$ and resolutions $p:P\to G$, $p':P'\to G'$, there is a map $\widetilde f:P\to P'$ with $p'\widetilde f$ chain homotopic to $fp$, and its homotopy class is unique. Identity and composition follow from this uniqueness. Taking $f=1$ in both directions shows any two resolutions of $G$ are canonically chain homotopy equivalent over $G$; taking $f$ a quasi-isomorphism shows its lift is a quasi-isomorphism. For semi-free $P,P'$, a quasi-isomorphism between them is a homotopy equivalence: apply the $H^0$ isomorphism first with source $P'$ to obtain a right inverse, then with source $P$ to obtain the other inverse identity. Apply this mapping-complex argument to right modules over $\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$, using the action conversion in step 3; these are exactly the left resolutions and left-module homotopies needed here.

source.place: Tag 09KM (dga-lemma-property-P-K-projective), Tag 09LS; mapping-complex cone and lifting calculations written explicitly, using the existing dg-category homotopical-projectivity statement.

proof.text: Balanced tensor preserves these homotopies. If $h$ is a right-module homotopy then $h\otimes1$ is the tensor homotopy; if $k$ is a left-module homotopy then on homogeneous tensors its formula is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes k(y)$. Substitution in $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes dy$ gives $dH+Hd$ equal to the desired difference of maps. For a right homotopy $h$, $h(xa)=h(x)a$; for a left homotopy $k$, $k(ay)=(-1)^{|a|}ak(y)$. These identities verify the balanced relation for the two displayed formulas. On any cycle $z$ the difference of the induced maps is $dH(z)$, so homotopic maps induce equal cohomology maps. Thus on maps define the derived tensor by $\widetilde f\otimes\widetilde g$ on $P\otimes Q$. Step 5 makes it independent of lifts and resolutions and compatible with composition; step 3 and homotopy equivalences show it inverts objectwise quasi-isomorphisms in each variable. Its canonical map to the ordinary tensor is $p\otimes q$. This verifies naturality, both-variable invariance and compatibility with the two one-input computations in step 4.

source.place: Tags 09LR (dga-lemma-bc-homotopy), 09LS, 09S3; tensor homotopy formulas checked directly.

proof.text: Now impose the extra flatness hypotheses. The formulas in the statement define the unnormalized bar complex: associativity gives $\partial_i\partial_j=\partial_{j-1}\partial_i$ for $i<j$, so the two orders of merging three neighboring factors cancel in the alternating sum and the horizontal differential squares to zero. Each face is a chain map for the internal tensor differential; hence $(-1)^n d_{V_n}$ anticommutes with the face differential, since a face changes $n$ to $n-1$. This proves $d_B^2=0$. Units give the degeneracies. On $V_1$, augmentation after $\partial_0-\partial_1$ is zero by the balanced relation; on other lengths its compatibility is immediate. Applying a module map to the end factor commutes with every face, internal differential and augmentation, so this is a natural construction.

source.place: Drinfeld 3.6(i), expanded by the worker: verification of the specific bar convention of this node.

proof.text: For any left module $F$, the augmentation $B(h_X,\mathcal B,F)\to F(X)$ is a homotopy equivalence. Include $F(X)$ as augmented simplicial degree $-1$. Define $s_{-1}(f)=1_X\otimes f$; on a bar tensor beginning with $a\in\mathcal B(U_n,X)$ define $s_n$ by prepending $1_X$ and treating $a$ as the newly inserted mapping-complex factor. Then $\partial_0s_n=1$ and $\partial_i s_n=s_{n-1}\partial_{i-1}$ for $i>0$, by the unit and associativity laws, including the augmentation at $n=0$. Consequently $bs+sb=1$ on the augmented horizontal complex, where $b$ is the alternating face differential. The maps $s_n$ commute with internal differentials before totalization; afterwards their internal contributions cancel because the total internal signs on lengths $n$ and $n+1$ are opposite. Thus on the unaugmented total complex $s$ gives $ds+sd=1-i\epsilon$, with $\epsilon i=1$ and $i(f)=1_X\otimes f$. For shifts, $B(h_X[k],\mathcal B,F)\cong B(h_X,\mathcal B,F)[k]$ multiplies the length-$n$ summand by $(-1)^{kn}$. Its internal differential matches by the right-shift convention, and this length sign makes the face differential match the outer shift sign $(-1)^k$. On a shifted complex a homotopy is multiplied by $(-1)^k$; conjugating that shifted contraction by this isomorphism gives the unit-insertion contraction for $h_X[k]$. Taking direct sums of these isomorphisms and homotopies gives the assertion for sums of shifted representables.

source.place: Drinfeld 3.6(i), bar contraction supplied explicitly by the worker; no flatness is used in the representable contraction.

proof.text: Let $P$ be an arbitrary semi-free right module. Filter $B(P,\mathcal B,F)$ and $P\otimes_{\mathcal B}F$ by $P_i$ and filter the cone of their augmentation correspondingly. Since $P_i\subset P_{i+1}$ is graded-split, tensoring its values with any of the other factors preserves that splitting and quotient, and so does the direct sum over strings and lengths. The successive cone quotients are the cones of the bar augmentations for $P_{i+1}/P_i$, which are acyclic by step 8. Step 2, induction from zero and then the union prove that the augmentation $B(P,\mathcal B,F)\to P\otimes_{\mathcal B}F$ is a quasi-isomorphism, for every $F$. Finite support of tensors and bar lengths identifies the unions with the full complexes, so this argument imposes no boundedness. In particular $B(P,\mathcal B,Q)\to P\otimes_{\mathcal B}Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09S3 split-filtration argument, applied to the explicit augmented bar cones of step 8; worker expansion of Drinfeld 3.6(i).

proof.text: We check the flatness and unbounded-totalization issue needed for the other comparison. If $K,L$ are homotopically flat over $\mathbf Z$, then $K\otimes L$ is so: for acyclic $A$, first $L\otimes A$ is acyclic and then $K\otimes(L\otimes A)$ is acyclic; reassociate pure tensors. A shifted complex is homotopically flat with $K$, and sums preserve this property by the finite-support argument of step 2. A graded-split exhaustive filtration whose quotient complexes are homotopically flat also has homotopically flat union: tensor with an arbitrary acyclic $A$, keep the splitting and quotient, and apply the induction and union argument of step 2. Applying this at each object to the semi-free filtrations shows that $P$ and $Q$ are objectwise homotopically flat, because their representable quotient values are sums of shifted mapping complexes and these are flat by the added hypothesis. Finally a tensor with a homotopically flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms: its tensor with the cone is acyclic, and tensor commutes with that cone up to the Koszul signs, so step 2 applies.

source.place: Drinfeld 3.3 definition; all flatness-closure assertions here are proved from that definition and the split-filtration cycle argument.

proof.text: Suppose first that $F$ is objectwise homotopically flat. For $p:P\to G$, in each fixed simplicial degree the map $V_n(P,\mathcal B,F)\to V_n(G,\mathcal B,F)$ is a quasi-isomorphism: each summand tensors $p(U_n)$ with finitely many homotopically flat mapping complexes and $F(U_0)$, so step 10 applies; then take their direct sum. To pass from columns to the direct-sum total, filter the cone of the bar map by lengths $0\leq n\leq r$. Faces decrease length, so these are subcomplexes; the quotient at length $r$ is a shift of the acyclic column cone. Step 2 gives acyclicity by induction in $r$ and by the union. Thus $B(P,\mathcal B,F)\to B(G,\mathcal B,F)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $B(P,\mathcal B,Q)\to B(P,\mathcal B,F)$, each column tensors $q(U_0)$ with $P(U_n)$ and the mapping-complex factors, all homotopically flat by step 10. Its column cone is acyclic; filtering the total cone by length gives acyclic shifted column quotients, so induction and union in step 2 prove the claimed quasi-isomorphism. If instead only $G$ is objectwise flat, factor the comparison in the other order: $B(P,\mathcal B,Q)\to B(G,\mathcal B,Q)\to B(G,\mathcal B,F)$. For the first arrow, each column tensors $p(U_n)$ with the flat mapping factors and $Q(U_0)$, which is flat by step 10. For the second, each column tensors $q(U_0)$ with the flat mapping factors and $G(U_n)$, which is flat by this case hypothesis. Thus every column cone is acyclic in each arrow; their total cones have the length filtration with acyclic shifted column quotients, and step 2 proves both total cones acyclic. This explicitly handles arbitrarily unbounded internal cochain degrees without a spectral-sequence convergence claim.

source.place: Drinfeld 3.6(i), generalized module comparison proved by the worker; finite-length cone filtration replaces any convergence assertion.

proof.text:
Combining steps 9 and 11 gives the natural comparison span
$$B(G,\mathcal B,F)\ \longleftarrow\ B(P,\mathcal B,Q)\ \longrightarrow\ P\otimes_{\mathcal B}Q.$$
Both arrows are quasi-isomorphisms, and the right-hand object is the derived balanced tensor of steps 4–6. The arrows commute with augmentation to $G\otimes_{\mathcal B}F$, since every component uses only $p,q$, actions and composition. For a module map lift it to the resolutions as in step 5: the resulting squares commute up to chain homotopy. Explicitly write a homogeneous length-$n$ tensor as $x\otimes a_n\otimes\cdots\otimes a_1\otimes y$. A homotopy $h$ of right-module maps gives the internal homotopy $h(x)\otimes a_n\otimes\cdots\otimes a_1\otimes y$; a homotopy $k$ of left-module maps gives $(-1)^{|x|+\sum_j|a_j|}x\otimes a_n\otimes\cdots\otimes a_1\otimes k(y)$. The graded module identities in step 6 show that these commute with every face: at the right-action face use $h(xa)=h(x)a$, and at the left-action face use $k(ay)=(-1)^{|a|}ak(y)$; the other faces just merge unaffected adjacent factors. Multiply either internal homotopy by $(-1)^n$ on length $n$. Its internal contribution to $dH+Hd$ is the difference of the end maps; the two face contributions cancel since the signs at lengths $n$ and $n-1$ are opposite. For two varying ends, decompose the difference as $(f-f')\otimes g+f'\otimes(g-g')$ and add the two homotopies, with the unchanged end acted on by the indicated chain map. Consequently the comparison is independent of lifts and natural for maps between pairs satisfying the stated flatness condition, even when different end factors supply flatness. The shift identity $(V_n[n])[1]=V_n[n+1]$ gives exactly $n+1$ suspensions in $B[1]$, finishing the last clause.
